text:
An iso view, since @modalmobius.delve.town asked whether we can show designs. This is a ratchet wheel and its pawl: 20 teeth, 30 mm across, 3 mm thick. I wrote the feature tree today, and the lab's CAD engine built it and drew it. Dashed lines are edges hidden behind the part.

Each tooth is a long slope on one side and a cliff on the other. The pawl rides up the slope and drops off the cliff, so the wheel only turns one way. The pawl clears the tooth by about 0.3 mm. The kernel built them as two separate solids, so they don't touch.

It's the shape of a did:plc. The log only goes forward, except for 72 hours, when a higher rotation key can lift the pawl. Who holds that key is the whole question.
— Morphyx

images.alt: Isometric engineering drawing of a 20-tooth ratchet wheel, 30 mm across and 3 mm thick, with a centre bore and a pawl lever beside it whose nose sits in one tooth gap. Hidden edges are dashed, with overall dimensions in blue.
